scope: All nine fresh Java-valid inputs dispatch as Rust Component and have valid Java/Rust SVGs. Eight conventional command-order cases pass; the public !procedure expansion rejects the mechanism.

inputs.result: PASS: named root note data-source-line is 2 on both sides.
PASS: the initially blank first body record gives data-source-line 4 on both sides.
PASS: attached root note data-source-line is 3 and GMN/entity IDs agree.
PASS: nested attached note data-source-line is 5 and its owner-qualified GMN5 agrees.
PASS: the first of multiple named body records supplies data-source-line 2.
PASS: the first of multiple attached body records supplies data-source-line 3.
PASS: inline note remains at command data-source-line 2.
PASS: normal execution order and first-body provenance both yield ent0002, ent0003, ent0004.

FAIL: both sides correctly give the procedure body note data-source-line 3, but Java executes the preceding source-line-6 component first (ProcedureWorkerC ent0002, ProcedureLocationC ent0003). Rust sorts events by provenance and reverses them (ProcedureLocationC ent0002, ProcedureWorkerC ent0003).

implementation_audit.java_provenance: Both CommandFactoryNote and CommandFactoryNoteOnEntity remove the opener before obtaining BlocLines.getLocation(), while command execution and unique-sequence allocation remain in preprocessor-expanded execution order.
implementation_audit.rust_provenance: crates/rustuml-parser/src/parse/component.rs:346-354 and 402-407 correctly retain the first mapped body record. However crates/rustuml-render/src/component.rs:489-538 sorts all UID events by source_line, conflating metadata provenance with Java execution order.
implementation_audit.anti_overfit: The implementation has no fixture-shaped conditionals, golden reads, comparator/baseline changes, post-hoc SVG metadata rewrite, or new unexplained parity constants. The failure comes from a missing execution-order model exposed by a public TIM feature.

findings.title: Mapped body provenance must not reorder Java UID allocation
findings.java_location: CommandFactoryNote.createMultiLine / CommandFactoryNoteOnEntity.createMultiLine and the observed !procedure execution order
findings.impact: Valid public preprocessor input produces swapped entity IDs, violating the account's claimed source-ordered UID/emission behavior even though data-source-line itself is correct.

residue: The unrelated multiline note-on-link path retains arithmetic current_line + 1 and was not scored because this account claims named and attached Component notes only.
conclusion: REJECTED. First-body provenance is correct in ordinary inputs, including blank first body records, but the model must carry a separate execution ordinal before it can coexist with Java-compatible UID allocation through TIM expansion.
